Hajdudorog Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Újtelep utca 2, Hungary

Not demolished. Founded by the Harstein family between 1848 and 1850, Hajdúdorog's Jewish community maintained this cemetery from as early as 1849 through 1950. Few Jews survived the Holocaust here, and in a particularly grim act of desecration, Torah scrolls were reportedly cut apart to make shoe insoles before eventually being buried in the cemetery. Survivor Samuel Reichmann sold the former community's synagogue in 1957; the cemetery itself is now maintained by the Heritage Foundation for Preservation of Jewish Cemeteries.
